## Isle of Man — Locality Guide (1840–1880)

**Jurisdiction:** British Crown dependency; 17 parishes; records kept at parish level. Key parishes for this project: Lezayre (Susanna Dawson born c.1840), Andreas (John Kneale born c.1839), Maughold (includes Ramsey, where family lived 1861–1877).

### Civil Registration Timeline
- Births/deaths: civil registration began **1878**
- Marriages: civil registration began **1884**
- Pre-1878/1884: Church of England parish registers are the sole official source

### FamilySearch Collections
| Collection | CID | Access | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Isle of Man, Parish Registers, 1598-2009 | 1784428 | Index + images | Preferred: current, maintained |
| Isle of Man, Marriages, 1606–1911 | 1711668 | Index only | Legacy; verify vs. 1784428 |
| Isle of Man, Births and Baptisms, 1607-1910 | 1708663 | Index only | Legacy |
| Isle of Man, Deaths and Burials, 1844-1918 | 1708590 | Index only | |

### Marriage Records
- Couples married in bride's parish; search Lezayre first
- No marriage license paperwork survived; banns were the norm
- From mid-1800s: register entries include fathers' names and occupations of both parties — key for paternity research
- External: FindMyPast IoM Marriages 1598-1979 ($); Ancestry Marriage Index 1606-1984 ($); IoMFHS index 1576-1960 (free)

### Baptism Records
- Church of England baptism registers name child, father (with occupation/residence from mid-1800s), and mother's given name (not maiden name)
- FamilySearch CID 1708663 (legacy index) and CID 1784428 (index + images)

### Census
- IoM-specific censuses 1841-1921 indexed at Ancestry ($) only
- FamilySearch 1871/1881 England & Wales censuses cover IoM residents

### Probate / Wills
- IoMFHS wills index 1576-1960 (free); Ancestry wills index 1600-1864 ($)
- FamilySearch Catalog has microfilm images (browse-only)

### Newspapers
- Isle of Man Newspapers 1792-1960 at imuseum.im ($) — useful for marriage notices

### Other
- ManxBMD.com: free online index for births, marriages, deaths
- Volume_search: 3,848 volumes for IoM 1840-1880, most 0% indexed (browse-only fallback)

entry.rationale: FamilySearch collection 'Isle of Man, Marriages, 1606–1911' (CID 1711668) is the first-stop name-indexed source for IoM church marriages. Search for bride surname Dawson (and variants: Dason, Dawsone) to find Susanna. Civil registration of marriages did not begin until 1884, so this pre-1878 marriage will be in church registers. Note: this is a legacy index-only collection; any match must be verified against original images in CID 1784428. IoM marriage registers from the mid-1800s onward include fathers' names, so a positive result may simultaneously answer q_002.

FamilySearch 'Isle of Man, Parish Registers, 1598-2009' (CID 1784428) is the current, maintained collection with both index and images. Per loc_001: couples typically married in the bride's parish, and Susanna was born in Lezayre — search Lezayre parish marriage entries first, c.1858–1862. This collection is the preferred source over the legacy CID 1711668 because it is actively maintained and provides access to original images for verification.

Isle of Man Family History Society (iomfhs.im) maintains a free marriage index covering 1576–1960. Searching this independent index (compiled from the same parish register base) provides a cross-check against the FamilySearch legacy index. URL: https://www.iomfhs.im/resources/marriages/index_marriages.html. Route to search-external-sites for execution.

Search for the baptism of Thomas Kneale (born 1861 in Lezayre, son of John Kneale and Susanna Dawson Kneale) in CID 1708663 'Isle of Man, Births and Baptisms, 1607-1910'. The baptism entry will name both parents; the father's name establishes paternity (aiding q_002) and the date establishes a terminus ante quem for the marriage. This is a FAN-adjacent search (child's record as evidence about the parents). Susanna is named as 'Susanna Dawson Kneale' in the 1878 baptism of William (already in tree sources), establishing the maiden name pattern.

Ancestry 'Isle of Man, Marriage Index, 1606-1984' (collection 9218) is a Manx National Heritage index accessible via Ancestry. Provides an independent search path for the Kneale–Dawson marriage when FamilySearch indexes yield no result. Subscription required ($). Route to search-external-sites.

1861 Isle of Man census (Ancestry, $) will show John and Susanna Kneale with son Thomas (age ~0). Their presence as a married couple with a Lezayre-born child confirms the marriage occurred before April 1861 and may record their parish of residence at census time — useful corroboration and may narrow the search window for the marriage register. Route to search-external-sites.

Search FamilySearch 'Isle of Man, Births and Baptisms, 1607-1910' (CID 1708663) for Susanna Dawson's baptism circa 1838-1842 in Lezayre. IoM Church of England baptism registers name the child's father (and mother's given name); a baptism entry is direct parentage evidence. Susanna's maiden name 'Dawson' is confirmed by multiple sources including the 1878 baptism of son William. Note: pli_001 (marriage register search for q_001) may also name her father if a mid-1800s register entry is found, since those routinely include both fathers' names; both searches are complementary.

If the CID 1708663 index yields no result (legacy collection, partial coverage), browse Lezayre parish baptism images directly in CID 1784428 'Isle of Man, Parish Registers, 1598-2009' (index + images). Reading the Lezayre baptism register pages for 1838-1842 page-by-page will surface any unbaptised or misindexed entry for Susanna Dawson. This is the highest-reliability source for the original register content.

1841 Isle of Man census (Ancestry, collection D8981, $) taken 6 June 1841. Susanna Dawson would be approximately 1 year old and should appear with her father's household. The 1841 census records name and approximate age for each household member; identifying her father's name from the household context is the goal. This is the earliest census that could show her with her father. Route to search-external-sites.

1851 Isle of Man census (Ancestry, $). Susanna Dawson would be approximately 11 years old and almost certainly still living in her father's household. The 1851 census provides full names and ages, making positive identification more reliable than the 1841 round-age census. If her father is found here, subsequent searches can confirm his identity and add corroborating detail. Route to search-external-sites.

Isle of Man Family History Society (iomfhs.im) free births index covers 1576-1960. An independent cross-check of the Dawson baptism entries for Lezayre circa 1838-1842; may surface variants not caught by the FS legacy index. URL: https://www.iomfhs.im/resources/births/index_births.html. Route to search-external-sites.

Dedicated search for the marriage of Susanna's parents to each other — a distinct item required by BCG Standard 14 for parentage questions. Once the father's name is identified from the baptism or census, search for a Dawson marriage in Lezayre/IoM c.1830-1845 in CID 1711668 and CID 1784428. The parents' marriage record: (a) confirms the couple as a unit; (b) supplies Susanna's mother's maiden name, which census records omit; (c) by its date relative to Susanna's birth, corroborates paternity evidence from the baptism or census. Note: the couple's marriage proves they married — it does not by itself establish Susanna as their child; that link requires her baptism or a census co-residence with the parents.

## Proof Summary: Marriage of Susanna Dawson and John Kneale

**Conclusion:** The evidence strongly suggests that Susanna Dawson married John Kneale on **21 October 1860** at **Lezayre, Isle of Man** (*probable* tier). Original register image examination would advance this conclusion to proved.

### Evidence

**CID 1784428 indexed record (primary evidence).** An indexed entry in "Isle of Man, Parish Registers, 1598-2009" records the marriage of John Kneale and Susanna Dawson on 21 October 1860 at Lezayre, Isle of Man.^[1] The officiating minister or parish clerk who created the register entry acted in an official capacity with first-hand knowledge of the event (information: primary; evidence: direct). Access was via FamilySearch's indexed transcription; the source is therefore classified as derivative. The underlying physical register is held by the Isle of Man Civil Registry, Douglas; a digital image of the register page is accessible at ark:/61903/3:1:S3HY-65T3-MR8 but was not examined in this research session.

**CID 1711668 legacy index (discovery source).** A legacy derivative index, "Isle of Man, Marriages, 1606-1911," also records the same marriage at Lezayre on 21 October 1860.^[2] Compiled circa 2010 from FHL microfilm of the same Lezayre parish register, this index is not independent of the CID 1784428 entry — both trace to the same physical document. It served as the discovery source and confirms no discrepancy was introduced in the CID 1784428 transcription, but it adds no independent corroboration of the date or place.

**CID 1708663 christening record (independent corroboration).** An entry in "Isle of Man, Births and Baptisms, 1607-1910" records the christening of Thomas Henry Kneale on 9 December 1860 at Lezayre, Isle of Man, naming John Kneale as father and Susanna Dawson as mother.^[3] This is an original source (a distinct parish register for a different life event) with primary information from the presenting parents, independently created forty-nine days after the claimed marriage date. Its contribution is indirect: it establishes that John Kneale and Susanna Dawson were a married couple with a child by 9 December 1860, consistent with a marriage on 21 October 1860, but it does not itself state the marriage date.

### Analysis and Correlation

The CID 1784428 and CID 1711668 records agree on date (21 October 1860) and place (Lezayre) but derive from a single physical register and count as one evidence unit. The CID 1708663 christening is fully independent — different record type, different event, different informants — and corroborates the marriage as having occurred before 9 December 1860. No contradictory evidence was encountered: no second marriage record for either party under variant names, and no record suggesting a different date or parish.

### Tier and Limitation

The marriage date and place rest on indexed derivative records of the Lezayre parish register. The original register image was not independently read. A second independent original source directly stating the date is not available from the searched collections. The evidence strongly points to 21 October 1860, Lezayre — no competing date or place exists — but the absence of original image examination holds the conclusion at *probable*. Examining the register image at ark:/61903/3:1:S3HY-65T3-MR8 and confirming the indexed date against the handwritten entry would advance the conclusion to proved.

entry.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Summary: Father of Susanna Dawson

**Conclusion:** The evidence strongly suggests that **John Dawson** was the father of Susanna Dawson, born circa March 1839 at Lezayre, Isle of Man, who later married John Kneale (*probable* tier). Examination of the original register images would advance this conclusion to proved.

### Evidence

**1839 Lezayre Christening Register (primary evidence — original source).** The Lezayre christening register records the christening of Susanna Dawson on 10 March 1839, naming "John Dawson" as father and "Jane Corlett" as mother.^[1] This entry is classified as an original source (CID 1784428, "Isle of Man, Parish Registers, 1598-2009"). The informant for the father's name is John Dawson himself, who appeared as one of the presenting parents — primary information, direct evidence. This is the most authoritative evidence for the father's identity, created at or near the time of Susanna's birth. A digital image of the register page is noted in the citation detail (ark:/61903/3:1:9396-CBL3-F) but was not independently examined in this session.

**1860 Lezayre Marriage Register (independent corroborating evidence — derivative source).** The Lezayre marriage register entry for Susanna Dawson's marriage to John Kneale on 21 October 1860 names "John Dawson" as the bride's father.^[2] The informant is Susanna Dawson herself, providing primary information from her own self-reported parentage at the time of her marriage. Evidence type: direct. This source is classified as derivative in this project (accessed via FamilySearch's indexed transcription; original image not independently examined). It is independent of the 1839 christening — different event, different year (twenty-one years later), and different informant (the daughter rather than the father). Susanna's naming of the same man as her father at an event requiring her to declare her own identity strengthens the identification.

**1832 Ballaugh Marriage Register (contextual corroboration — original source).** The Ballaugh marriage register records the marriage of John Dawson and Jane Corlett on 16 August 1832 at Ballaugh, Isle of Man.^[3] This original source provides primary information from the officiating minister. It is not direct evidence of the Susanna-John Dawson parentage but contextually corroborates it: the same couple (John Dawson + Jane Corlett) named as Susanna's parents in the 1839 christening register were a married couple seven years before her birth, consistent with paternity. It also supplies the BCG-required parents' marriage record, confirming the couple's union and providing the mother's maiden name (Corlett).

### Analysis and Correlation

Two independent acts — the 1839 christening and the 1860 marriage — name "John Dawson" as Susanna's father. The informants differ: John Dawson himself (1839, presenting parent) and Susanna Dawson (1860, bride). The events are separated by twenty-one years and recorded in different register series for different life events. No competing candidate for Susanna's father appeared in any searched source. The parents' 1832 marriage (a third independent act) establishes the couple existed seven years before Susanna's birth and supplies the mother's maiden name (Corlett), which neither the marriage register nor later records provide.

### Tier and Limitation

One of the two direct-parentage sources (the 1860 marriage, src_002) is classified as derivative in this project — its index was accessed via FamilySearch rather than the original register image, and that image was not independently read. A proved tier requires two or more independent original sources with primary information directly agreeing on the specific fact. The 1839 christening register (original, primary, direct) meets that standard for a single source; a second independent original source directly stating the parentage has not been accessed in its original form. Examining the christening register image (ark:/61903/3:1:9396-CBL3-F) and the marriage register image (ark:/61903/3:1:S3HY-65T3-MR8) to confirm both indexed entries against the handwritten originals would advance the conclusion to proved.
